name: Mozambique
summary: A Portuguese colony that won independence in 1975 after a liberation war; a civil war followed until 1992.

knownFor.label: Island of Mozambique
knownFor.note: Old trading town, a World Heritage Site.

knownFor.label: AK-47 on the flag
knownFor.note: The only national flag with a modern rifle.

location.value: South-east Africa on the Indian Ocean; 801,590 km².

terrain.value: A long coastal plain in the south and centre, rising to highlands and mountains in the north and west.

climate.value: Tropical to subtropical, with a hot, wet season (November–April) and a cooler dry season.

resources.value: Natural gas and coal, aluminium, heavy sands, prawns and farmland.

disasters.value: Cyclone Idai (2019) and Cyclone Freddy (2023) caused deadly floods; droughts also recur.

population.value: 34,881,007 (2024 estimate, infobox); the body gives 34,777,605 for 2024.

urbanisation.value: Maputo is the capital and largest city; Beira and Nampula are other major towns.

disease.value: HIV and malaria are the main diseases, with cholera outbreaks after floods.

migration.value: Millions were displaced or became refugees during the civil war (1977–92); many have since returned.

economicBase.value: About 80% of people worked in mostly subsistence farming in 2013; aluminium is listed among industries; the Mamba South gas field in the Rovuma Basin has about 4,200 billion cubic metres of reserves.

tradeRoutes.value: The ports of Maputo, Beira and Nacala serve South Africa, Zimbabwe, Malawi and Zambia by rail and road.

wealth.value: GDP per person about $663 (nominal, 2025 estimate); HDI 0.493, low (183rd, 2023).

moneyAndTax.value: The metical, introduced in 1980 and replaced in 2006 at a rate of 1,000 old for 1 new.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: The infobox calls it a dominant-party semi-presidential republic under an authoritarian government, while the text calls it a relatively stable presidential republic; the president is directly elected for five years.

keyRulers.value: Samora Machel (first president, one-party Marxist state, died in a plane crash on 19 October 1986). Later and present leaders are not named here.

succession.value: One-party state under FRELIMO from 1975 to 1990; first multiparty elections in 1994.

institutions.value: The Assembly of the Republic (parliament), a strong presidency, and local government.

stability.value: Civil war from 1977 to 1992, with about one million deaths.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: The armed forces were formed from the FRELIMO and RENAMO fighters after the 1992 peace.

majorWars.value: Mozambican Civil War (1977–92): about one million deaths, and 300,000–600,000 deaths from famine during the war.

territoryChange.value: Mozambique’s borders have stayed the same since independence in 1975.

alliancesRivals.value: Joined the Commonwealth in 1995, though never a British colony; it also belongs to the Community of Portuguese-speaking Countries.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: Literacy has risen since independence but is still among the lower rates in Africa.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Railways run inland from the ports to Zimbabwe, Malawi and South Africa, though some lines were damaged in the war.

languageWriting.value: Portuguese is the official language; Makhuwa, Sena, Tsonga and many other Bantu languages are widely spoken.

artsArchitecture.value: Makonde wood carving, marrabenta music and Portuguese colonial buildings in Maputo and Ilha de Moçambique.

socialStructure.value: A society of many ethnic groups, with a small urban elite and most people farming.

sharedIdentity.value: The independence struggle (1964–74) is the main symbol of national unity.

dailyLife.value: Most families live in villages with simple houses; seafood and matapa (cassava leaves in coconut sauce) are common foods.

neighbours.value: Tanzania, Malawi, Zambia, Zimbabwe, South Africa, Eswatini.

ideasReligions.value: Marxism-Leninism was the official ideology until 1990, when a new constitution brought multi-party politics.

colonisation.value: Portuguese colonisation from 1505; a Portuguese colony until independence on 25 June 1975.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Mozambique continues as an independent republic.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
